q: 1. Material cost is concerned with ......
explain: Materials used directly in the work are a direct cost.

q: 2. Directed cost of a project is due to
options: Establishment charges as salaries of administrative staff
Cost of materials and wages of labour
explain: Direct cost of a project arises from costs directly attributable to production, such as the cost of materials and wages of labour.

q: 3. The benefit that is forgone by engaging the resource in a chosen activity instead of engaging the same resource in the forgone activity is known as :
explain: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative given up when a choice is made.

q: 4. The sunk cost includes
options: an invested capital that cannot be retrieved
explain: Sunk costs are historical costs that have already been incurred and cannot be recovered by any future decision.

q: 5. Total cost of project is sum of ......
explain: Total cost = fixed cost + variable cost.

q: 6. Which of the following is not direct cost for a project ?
explain: Insurance is an administrative or overhead expense (indirect cost) as it cannot be tied to a specific unit of production.

q: 7. Costs which are independent of output and no alteration by the change is production level are called
explain: Fixed costs remain static regardless of whether 1 unit or 1,000 units are produced.

q: 8. In economic marginal cost is the change in total cost that arises when the quantity produced changes by
explain: Marginal cost is defined as the cost of producing 'one additional' unit.

q: 9. The additional money received from selling one more unit at a specified level of output is
explain: Marginal revenue is the incremental increase in total revenue from selling one extra unit.

q: 10. The most unpredictable cost of a project is
explain: Geological uncertainties make underground work (tunnels, foundations) notoriously difficult to estimate accurately.

q: 11. Optimization of any project means selection of a project option corresponding to
explain: Key answer b: optimization picks the option with minimum cost. This key entry is blurry, so please verify.

q: 12. Prime cost of a project includes
explain: Prime cost is the sum of all direct costs involved in manufacturing or construction.

q: 13. Subsidy provided to private enterprises is taken as ...... for the financial analysis of any project.
explain: In financial analysis a subsidy received is treated as revenue (inflow) to the enterprise.

q: 14. In economics, the change in total cost that arises when the quantity produced changes by one unit is called :
explain: This is the classic definition of Marginal Cost.

q: 15. The project risk that will encounter due to earthquake in which both contracting parties are unable to control the situation is ......
explain: Force majeure covers events like earthquakes beyond the control of both contracting parties.

q: 16. Supervisor's cost is ......
explain: Supervision supports many activities and cannot be charged to one item, so it is an indirect cost.

q: 17. Insurance cost is ......
explain: Insurance covers the whole project, so it is an indirect cost.

q: 18. Fixed cost can be ......
explain: A fixed cost can be direct or indirect depending on whether it can be traced to a specific item.

q: 19. Variable cost can be ......
explain: A variable cost can be direct or indirect.

q: 20. Total cost is sum of ......
explain: Total cost can be split as direct + indirect, prime + overhead, or fixed + variable; all give the same total.

q: 21. The estimate based on a detailed quantity survey and furnishes the most accurate and reliable estimate possible is known as ......
explain: A definitive estimate is based on detailed quantity survey and is the most accurate.
